content.rendered:
Having disarmed the powers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross. Disarmed. Past tense. The believer today is not fighting an enemy at full strength. The believer is walking against an enemy who was stripped of his weapons two thousand years ago.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, July 23, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And having disarmed the powers and authorities, he made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross.”
Colossians 2:15 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Colossians 2 is one of the great victory passages of the New Testament. Paul is describing what Jesus accomplished at the cross, and he reaches for the imagery of a Roman triumph parade to describe it. In the ancient world, a Roman general returning from a successful campaign would march into Rome at the head of a triumphal procession. The captured enemies would be paraded through the streets in chains, stripped of their armor and weapons, publicly humiliated before the watching crowd. Paul says Jesus did that at the cross, but to the powers of darkness.

The Greek word Paul uses for “disarmed” is apekdusamenos. It literally means to strip off, to divest, to publicly remove the clothing and armor of. Jesus, at the cross, stripped the principalities and powers of the authority they had held over humanity. Their armor was taken. Their weapons were removed. The tools they had used to hold the human race in bondage were confiscated by the King who conquered them on Golgotha. And having disarmed them, He then paraded them publicly as defeated foes.

This is the picture that reorders spiritual conflict for the believer. The enemy the believer resists today is not an enemy at full military strength. The enemy has been publicly disarmed. What he has left is bluff. What he has left is deception. What he has left is intimidation. What he does not have left is legitimate authority over the believer who is in Christ. The cross took it. The cross settled it. The cross made a public spectacle of it. And the resurrection sealed the verdict for eternity.

This changes how the believer walks into spiritual conflict. When fear speaks, the believer hears it as a bluff from a disarmed enemy. When accusation comes, the believer hears it as the shouting of a public prisoner who has lost his weapons. When intimidation rises, the believer knows it is coming from powers whose armor is already stripped off. The enemy still exists. He still schemes. But he has been legally, publicly, historically defeated. The believer’s job is not to defeat him. Jesus already did. The believer’s job is to walk in the victory Jesus won.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is triumphant. You are not fighting an enemy at full strength. You are enforcing a victory that has already been won. The powers of darkness were disarmed at the cross. Every weapon they raise against you today is a weapon that has been repossessed by the King who conquered them. Walk in that victory today. It is yours in Christ.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that at the cross Jesus disarmed the powers and authorities, made a public spectacle of them, and triumphed over them. The enemy I face today is a defeated enemy. His armor has been stripped. His weapons have been confiscated. What he has left is bluff, and I refuse it in the name of Jesus. I do not fight for victory. I fight from victory. I walk today in the triumph the cross has already secured. Every accusation, every intimidation, every scheme is coming from a disarmed enemy, and I stand on the ground the Lord Jesus has already claimed. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The powers of darkness have been disarmed at the cross. The enemy I face today is a defeated enemy. I do not fight for victory. I fight from victory. Jesus has triumphed.
